quotes.text: The delegated permissions tie your automation to an actual human user. Under the hood, every API call is piggybacking on a real person's permissions and session.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains in two sentences why delegated permissions make background automation fragile.

quotes.text: Every action is tied back to the app's identity, not a person. Of course, app only permissions don't mean you throw out best practices. You still need to be smart about which specific permissions you select.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Balances the benefit of app-only access with the need for careful permission selection.

quotes.text: That secret is your app's identity card for Microsoft graph and exposing it even briefly is an open door for attackers.

quotes.text: Register the app, pick only application permissions, secure and regularly rotate your secrets and confirm admin consent actually went through. Get this chain right, and your automation becomes both safer and almost completely self sufficient.

takeaways: Delegated permissions tie automations to a real user's session, password and license, so background jobs break when that person changes roles, resets a password or leaves.
App-only permissions give an application its own identity in Microsoft Graph, enabling least-privilege access, unattended runs and cleaner audit trails.
A reliable setup requires registering the app, choosing only the needed application permissions, confirming admin consent and storing and rotating secrets securely.
hook: Your Microsoft 365 automations keep failing at 2 AM because they run on a user's delegated permissions. This episode is for admins and developers building custom Graph integrations who want background jobs that survive password resets and staff turnover. Learn how app-only permissions, app registrations and proper consent make automation secure and reliable.
